problems.description: app.py declares module-level constants in lower case; repo convention (and the seed it replaced) uses UPPER_CASE module-level constants.

test_app.py and conftest.py declare classes in non-PascalCase (2 violations each: class naming + module-level constant casing) — 4 of the 5 reported convention violations live in the test layer, contradicting the repo rule 'PascalCase classes'.

The commit wholesale-replaces the seed's multi-file Blueprint structure with a single-file app.py (~145 LOC) that merges client registry, broadcast, and message handling into one module, deleting the seed's existing organization and tests.
SonarQube delta shows +3 smells and +13 cognitive complexity in the new code — rising complexity in a deliberately flat single-module design.

strengths: Zero new bugs and zero duplication (SonarQube: bugs +0, duplications +0.0%)
Requirement-complete: per-client ID assignment, broadcast, disconnect cleanup, and the GET /health endpoint returning connected-client count are all implemented
Ships a test suite in session 1 (+3 files, conftest.py + test_app.py)
commit_reviews.summary: A requirement-complete, bug-free greenfield first session that delivers the notification-service story goal plus tests, but flattens the seed's modular structure into a single file and accumulates 5 naming-convention violations (convention score 0.72).

problems.description: Inconsistent message schema: the channel is read from the top-level envelope (`data.get("channel")`) for `broadcast` but from `payload.get("channel")` for `subscribe`/`unsubscribe` — two locations for the same concept invites API drift.

Broadcast envelope construction (timestamp + type) is duplicated between the channel and all-clients branches instead of being factored into a helper (contributing to the +19 cognitive complexity delta).
The commit adds a new feature (ChannelRegistry + subscribe/unsubscribe/broadcast + two HTTP endpoints) but touches zero test files — no coverage for the new channel behavior.

Measured convention score 0.72 is dragged down mostly by violations in conftest.py and test_app.py, which are NOT part of this diff — the app.py module-level constant violation may also be pre-existing. The actual added code follows conventions well.

strengths: ChannelRegistry closely mirrors the existing ClientRegistry pattern (threading.Lock, symmetric subscribe/unsubscribe/get methods), so it slots into the codebase idiomatically.
Clean cleanup path — remove_client_from_all in the finally block guarantees no stale channel membership on disconnect.
Thread-safety is handled consistently; get_subscribers returns a defensive copy, and empty channels are pruned.
commit_reviews.summary: A coherent, pattern-following feature addition that mirrors the existing registry idiom, but carries minor maintainability warts (schema inconsistency, duplicated envelope logic) and adds no tests for the new channel paths; the measured 0.72 convention score overstates the diff's own violations since most flagged files (conftest.py, test_app.py) are untouched by this commit.

compounding_issues: Subscription session limit (Claude quota, 'resets 2am Europe/Berlin') aborted sessions 3-5 — the integration, refactor, and cross-cutting commits are empty placeholder commits (0 tokens, 0 tool calls) carrying only .instrument/session.jsonl files, so the planned arc never materialized

Session 2's channel feature shipped with zero new tests (test_app.py unchanged at 13 tests) and exited non-zero mid-feature, leaving untested channel routing/registries as the foundation later sessions would have built on

Session 1 committed after a 383-line rewrite without running the test suite in-session (tests_passed 0/0); the post-hoc deep evaluator reported correctness 0.0 with evaluator_source 'unavailable', so the greenfield result was never independently verified

Early concurrency choice mixed threading.Lock-protected registries with asyncio (cyclomatic complexity 119, code_quality_score 0.117) — a maintainability burden cemented in session 1 that the aborted refactor session was meant to address
key_decisions: Session 1 fully rewrote the 250-line seed (383 lines changed) into an aiohttp-HTTP + websockets dual-stack server with a conftest.py async fixture harness, rather than extending the seed incrementally
Adopted a threading.Lock-serialized ClientRegistry/ChannelRegistry (thread-safety over a pure async design), accepting cross-concurrency-model complexity from the start

Session 2 added a ChannelRegistry with per-channel subscribe/unsubscribe routing and REST channel/subscriber endpoints, treating 'channel' as an optional broadcast field to preserve backward compatibility
The runner committed session states even on exit code 1 (session 2) and emitted empty commits for the quota-blocked sessions 3-5, cementing partial/placeholder states as permanent history
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality opened strong: session 1 delivered a complete, well-structured greenfield build (async server, thread-safe registries, a 13-test harness, 46 tool calls, $0.53) and session 2 added a sensible channel-subscription feature with clean REST endpoints — but that feature arrived untested and the session was cut off mid-work (exit 1). The remaining three sessions produced nothing: each died on the Claude subscription session limit within ~2 seconds at zero cost, yielding empty commits. The arc is a two-session story wearing a five-session mask — competence in what was built, but the integration/refactor/cross-cutting legs that would have hardened or vindicated it never executed, so the measured trajectory is flat-then-truncated rather than improving.
story_review.summary: A promising greenfield start and a coherent feature session collapse into three quota-killed empty commits, leaving an untested channel feature and a truncated 2-of-5-session story that never reached integration, refactor, or cross-cutting.
